## Trial `internal-dns-resolution-alpine__jUnGMR8`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** Both material outcomes of the task are satisfied with direct, verified evidence: node1 runs dnsmasq resolving inventory-api.internal to node2's IP while forwarding other queries upstream, and node2 is configured with node1 as its DNS resolver via a persistence-safe resolv.conf/dhcpcd.conf setup. The mandatory restart-evidence protocol was executed correctly on both nodes with matching boot-identity baselines and post-restart values in the fixed lifecycle snapshots, and DNS functionality was shown intact after each reboot. The only notable hygiene item is a brief, fully-reverted chattr +i/-i experiment on node2's resolv.conf.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.900 | 0.920 | 18/16 |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **node1-dns-resolver — Satisfied:** node1 runs an internal DNS resolver that resolves inventory-api.internal to node2's IP
  - **Why:** dnsmasq was installed and configured on node1 with address=/inventory-api.internal/10.100.231.11 and server=10.100.231.1 for upstream forwarding. Service was enabled and started (rc-service dnsmasq start, status: started), confirmed listening on 127.0.0.1:53 and 10.100.231.10:53. Direct nslookup against 10.100.231.10 resolved inventory-api.internal to 10.100.231.11 and google.com resolved correctly via upstream forwarding, both before and after a full node1 reboot (post-restart boot_id db97d71d... confirmed, service and resolution reverified).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-e004f10f0d454391`, `cmd-738b7803b04d41a4`, `cmd-434b789d04e745a6`, `cmd-64dbb7c27f174311`, `cmd-b21e10b326374e7c`, `global:after_executor:node1:listening-sockets`
- **node2-uses-node1-resolver — Satisfied:** node2 is configured to use node1 as its DNS resolver for internal lookups
  - **Why:** node2's /etc/resolv.conf was set to 'nameserver 10.100.231.10' and dhcpcd's resolv.conf hook was disabled (nohook resolv.conf) to prevent DHCP from overwriting it, verified to survive a dhcpcd service restart. nslookup from node2 resolved inventory-api.internal to 10.100.231.11 and google.com resolved externally, both before and after a full node2 reboot (post-restart boot_id 503293e9... confirmed, resolv.conf and resolution reverified).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-3b52ee8236a64492`, `cmd-4f7ebbb8127b4945`, `cmd-887256c3a08a45e7`, `cmd-21ce6514ec2941ba`, `cmd-2e5cd270820a4564`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.900**. One bounded, low-risk mutation not clearly tied to a required outcome: the executor set the immutable attribute on /etc/resolv.conf (chattr +i, cmd-4f7ebbb8127b4945) to protect against dhcpcd overwrites, then removed it before restarting dhcpcd to test persistence (chattr -i, cmd-887256c3a08a45e7). This was fully reverted and left no residue — the working persistence mechanism ultimately relied on the 'nohook resolv.conf' dhcpcd.conf entry, not the immutable flag. Fixed lifecycle diffs show only expected changes (new boot_id, dnsmasq listening sockets on node1, /tmp/reboot.log artifacts on both nodes from the self-scheduled reboot trick) with no damaged package state (apk check output unchanged) or abandoned services.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-4f7ebbb8127b4945`, `cmd-887256c3a08a45e7`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node1:package-health`, `global:after_executor:node2:package-health`
